It IS a reason to apply ORCHESTRATOR.md §5's PARTIAL/PASS semantics honestly: a finding that does not make the text WRONG, and does not mislead an agent into a wrong action, is recorded in `result.issues` for a later run rather than converted into a blocking verdict. Two questions, both yours: does the amended test now admit all four table rows (check each of the four against it, individually), and does the widening let anything in that should be out — in particular, does 'an explicit registry.json mid-work statement' remain decidable, or does it re-introduce the judgement call the test exists to remove? If the test is still wrong, that is a genuine FAIL; if it is right or merely imperfect-but-decidable, say which.

(3) WF02-REQ019's PLACEMENT. DOC-UPDATER places it OUT of class and reports the evidence: clause 1 holds (`orchestrator.log:49` carries the TEST-RUNNER dispatch) but clause 2 fails — commit `2682e06`'s subject is 'commit orchestrator.log Step 4 dispatch entry from interrupted run', i.e. ORCH committing its own line rather than the agent's work; `git log --all` over 04:50-05:15Z on 2026-08-16 returns zero commits; and the only `step04-test-run.json` is the re-dispatch, `created_at` 05:10:19Z. This placement is what stops the next re-derivation re-litigating the same incident, so it has to be right and it has to be legible.

(4) THE SIXTH-FIRING SENTENCE in anti-patterns entry 1. An entry that reads as an indictment is less likely to be followed than one that reads as a procedure.

ONE MORE TASK, AND IT IS YOURS ALONE. At Step 3f you correctly declined to edit your own COMPLETED, committed, attested result block in `step-03d-reviewer-regate.json`, on the ground that doing so is the exact act this run's amendment prohibits — and you routed it to ORCH as an appended correction. It does not bar the attesting agent from APPENDING a marked correction to its own attestation, which is the same shape as the `orch_timestamp_correction` precedent and strictly better than ORCH editing your words. result.summary:
PASS. Gate held to the scope I set at Step 3f: only 4.1(b)'s member sentence + its new table row, and 4.1's membership test + reworded exclusion sentence were re-reviewed. Everything else re-confirmed structurally rather than by recomputing DOC-UPDATER's hashes -- `git diff 0bbb2cc 57fd10d -- docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md` is exactly TWO hunks (@@ -379 and @@ -468), so section 2's fence, 4.1(a), 4.1(d) and the four-row death table (lines ~365-375) all fall OUTSIDE both hunks and are byte-identical between the two commits. That is a stronger check than reproducing a hash whose derivation method I would have had to trust, so I did not spot-confirm the hash values; the property they were offered to prove is proved directly. numstat: HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md 80/11, anti-patterns.md 18/0.

=== (1) 4.1(b) MEMBER SET -- PASS, AND THE RULE WAS CHECKED AGAINST THE INSTANCE ===
Rule side, all three required changes present (HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md:521-550): line 522 now reads "an object with **the six REQUIRED members below, and at most the one OPTIONAL member `backfill_note`**"; a seventh table row (line 534) defines `backfill_note` as "present **only** on a file amended under this subsection's single named exception below ... Admissible on no other file"; and lines 547-550 record the exception as SPENT -- "It authorised one named file (below) and no other, so **no further handoff can acquire this member**". The closure paragraph (536-545) also states the two rejected alternatives (six-as-minimum; folding into `reason`), which is what stops the next writer re-opening the enumeration.

Instance side -- verified, not accepted. `json.load` over handoffs/WF03-ISS0109-20260821/step-final-git-merge.json returns not_agent_attested keys EXACTLY ['reconstructed_by','reconstructed_at','reason','fields_written','evidence','not_verifiable_after_the_fact','backfill_note'] -- the six required, in the table's order, plus the one permitted optional, and nothing else. Its `backfill_note` supplies each of the three things the new row demands: what was renamed/added (orch_reconstruction -> not_agent_attested, commands_run -> evidence, fields_written added), by which run (WF03-ISS0117-20260821 step 3e, DOC-UPDATER), and the attestation that no factual assertion changed ("no factual assertion in this file was added, removed or reworded, verified by diffing the parsed structure before and after the edit"). The normative table and its single instance now agree, which was the whole defect.

Spent-ness verified independently: a scan of all 553 *.json under handoffs/ finds `not_agent_attested` as a top-level key on EXACTLY ONE file -- that one. The other four grep hits for `backfill_note` are handoff files that merely DISCUSS the field in prose (03e, 03f, 03g, and my own 03h task text), not carriers. No second file has acquired the member.

=== (2) RULING ON DOC-UPDATER'S WIDENING OF CLAUSE 2 -- UPHELD. THE WIDENING IS CORRECT AND WAS NECESSARY ===
My Step 3f test was WRONG AS WRITTEN and DOC-UPDATER was right to depart from it. Applied literally, "a handoff file, a commit, or an orchestrator.log line of its own" excludes WF02-REQ038 -- whose death, by my own Step 3f finding, survives ONLY as prose in registry.json. A membership test that expels a row of the very table it governs reproduces this run's defect one level further down. The lead-in DOC-UPDATER wrote makes the reasoning explicit rather than burying it ("Clause 2 is the one that does the work, and it is deliberately satisfiable by prose ... a test that demanded a file-shaped artefact would exclude a row already in the table"). I withdraw my formulation in favour of the amended one.

ALL FOUR ROWS ADMITTED -- checked individually against the amended test, each registry quote verified verbatim by reading registry.json:
- WF02-REQ027-20260816: clause 1 by orchestrator.log:222 (`ORCH -> REVIEWER | Step 2d hard gate dispatched`) AND by handoffs/WF02-REQ027-20260816/step-02d-reviewer.json. Clause 2 by registry /runs/9 `step_2d_infra_restart` -- verbatim "The first REVIEWER dispatch was terminated mid-work by an infrastructure session limit" -- and independently by orchestrator.log:223 (RESTART), which reports the same. Two independent clause-2 witnesses. IN.
- WF02-REQ038-20260817: clause 1 by handoffs/WF02-REQ038-20260817/step-01b-code-design-validator.json, addressed to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (the run has NO DISPATCH lines in orchestrator.log at all -- its only log lines are 499-501, MERGE/RELEASE/DONE). Clause 2 by registry /runs/29/note -- verbatim "One infra-terminated CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR dispatch (connection error mid-work, zero commits, cleanly re-dispatched from scratch)". IN, and IN ONLY BY VIRTUE OF THE WIDENING. This row alone settles the ruling.
- WF02-REQ043-20260818: clause 1 by handoffs/WF02-REQ043-20260818/step-final-git-merge.json, addressed to ELIXIR-DEV and still `status: PENDING` with `result: null` on disk today (ISS-0192), exactly as the table's third row says. Clause 2 by registry /runs/34/note -- verbatim "Interrupted by a host power outage mid-rebase". IN.
- WF03-ISS0109-20260821: clause 1 by handoffs/WF03-ISS0109-20260821/step-final-git-merge.json. Clause 2 by registry /runs/57/note -- verbatim "Step Final's ELIXIR-DEV died on an API error AFTER the merge landed and before writing its result block" -- which is precisely the "(or after completing its side effects)" limb. IN.

DOES THE WIDENING LET ANYTHING IN THAT SHOULD BE OUT? No, and the hardest case proves it rather than dodges it. WF02-REQ019's registry /runs/2/note reads "This run was interrupted mid-pipeline when the host process exited after Step 4 dispatch" -- prose in registry.json, containing "mid-pipeline", about a run that WAS mid-work. A naive reading of the widened clause would drag it in. It does not get in, because clause 2 is scoped twice over in the text as committed: its lead-in requires "an artefact or record *about that agent*" (this note is about the HOST PROCESS and about ORCH's dispatch, not about TEST-RUNNER), and its closing sentence states "ORCH's own `DISPATCH` line is evidence of clause 1 and **never** of clause 2". The subject of the statement, not the presence of the word, is what decides.

DECIDABLE? YES -- decidable in practice, with one residual I am classifying NON-BLOCKING. Two readers applying the amended test to all five candidates (four rows plus REQ019, plus REQ025) get the same answer, because the deciding question is mechanical: does a record name THE DISPATCHED AGENT and place its death inside its own work? All four rows answer yes in the registry's own words; REQ019 answers no on the same reading; REQ025 fails clause 1 outright. That is not the judgement call the test was written to remove -- that call was "is this incident in a class we only named" -- it is a reading of a named field's subject, and the text works the single hardest instance in full so the reading is demonstrated rather than asserted. Residual (N1 below): "explicit statement ... mid-work" is prose-shaped, so a future note that is genuinely ambiguous about its subject would need a tiebreak, and the tiebreak currently lives in clause 2's lead-in phrase rather than as its own numbered clause. Imperfect-but-decidable, not wrong. NOT a FAIL.

=== (3) WF02-REQ019 PLACEMENT -- PASS. ALL THREE EVIDENCE ITEMS RE-VERIFIED FIRST-HAND ===
- orchestrator.log:49 -- verified verbatim: "DISPATCH | WF-02 | WF02-REQ019-20260816 | ORCH -> TEST-RUNNER | Step 4 test run dispatched". Clause 1 holds, as the text says.
- commit 2682e06 -- `git log -1 --format=%s 2682e06` -> "chore(REQ-019): commit orchestrator.log Step 4 dispatch entry from interrupted run". Verified exact. ORCH committing its own dispatch line, authored 2026-08-16T10:08:31+05:00 (= 05:08:31Z), i.e. after the interruption, not agent work. orchestrator.log:50's RESUME line matches the quote too ("Committed and pushed the orphaned Step 4 dispatch log line (commit 2682e06)").
- `git log --all --since=2026-08-16T04:50:00Z --until=2026-08-16T05:15:00Z` -> ZERO commits. Verified.
- The fourth item, also checked: handoffs/WF02-REQ019-20260816/ holds exactly one step04-test-run.json, `created_at` 2026-08-16T05:10:19Z (started_at 05:09:09Z), and its task text does read "was interrupted before Step 4 could run". Both timestamps postdate the interruption and belong to the resumed session, so nothing in that directory is an artefact of the dead first dispatch. Clause 2 fails. Placement OUT of class is CORRECT.

Exclusion sentence non-exhaustive -- CONFIRMED, and in three independent places: the heading "**Known exclusions -- a record of what has been checked, NOT an exhaustive set**"; the explicit disclaimer "**This is not a claim that no third exists**"; and the forward instruction "anything newly surfaced is to be tested against the two clauses above rather than checked against this list". The prior text's "a **fifth** abnormal termination ... is deliberately **not** in this table", which read as exhaustive, is gone. The closing line "Both exclusions fail the test, so **neither is a fifth row and the four-row table above stands unchanged**" is consistent with my own re-verification. Legible: a reader hitting REQ019 in a future sweep finds the reasoning, the treatment trap ("redispatch is also what an unstarted dispatch gets") and the verdict in one place, so it does not get re-litigated.

=== (4) ANTI-PATTERNS ENTRY 1 -- PASS, PURE INSERTION, FRAMING IS MECHANISM NOT INDICTMENT ===
Pure-append confirmed by measurement, not by report: numstat 18/0 (ZERO deletions), a SINGLE hunk @@ -1009,6 +1009,24 @@, and 1070 -> 1088 lines. Zero deletions is dispositive that no existing entry's text was altered; the 18 lines land inside entry 1's own escalation narrative, after the fifth-firing paragraph and before "Why it is easy to miss", which is the correct home and leaves that paragraph reading coherently.

Framing verdict: MECHANISM, decisively. It names no agent as culpable, credits the finding to "the Step 3f gate" rather than blaming a producer, and explicitly extends the benefit of the doubt to every prior pass ("each move survived a re-derivation that was genuinely diligent *within the frame it inherited*"). The transferable content is stated as a procedure a reader can execute -- "name the level you are re-deriving at, and check the level above it once", with the count -> class -> exclusion-set trace as the evidence for why one level up is the right dose -- and it closes on the general law ("Re-deriving one level down from where the defect lives always confirms the defect") rather than on a tally. This reads as something an agent would follow. It is not an indictment.

=== FINDINGS, EACH CLASSIFIED ===
N1 (NON-BLOCKING). Clause 2's "about that agent" scoping is the tiebreak that keeps the widened test decidable -- it is what excludes WF02-REQ019 -- but it sits in the clause's lead-in prose rather than as its own numbered requirement. Does not make the text wrong (the scoping IS stated, twice, and the worked example demonstrates it) and cannot mislead an agent into a wrong action on any candidate now on record. Worth one clause in the next amendment that touches 4.1: promote "the record must name the dispatched agent as the party that died" to a numbered sub-clause of 2.
N2 (NON-BLOCKING). Clause 1 and clause 2 have asymmetric evidence lists: clause 2 now admits registry.json prose, clause 1 does not. For WF02-REQ038 the FIRST dispatch's only direct record is that registry note, so clause 1 is satisfied there via the redispatch's handoff file rather than the dead dispatch's -- sound (a redispatch presupposes a dispatch) and outcome-identical for all four rows, but the asymmetry is exactly the shape of gap this run keeps finding. One clause fixes it: add "or an explicit statement in registry.json that a dispatch was issued" to clause 1.
N3 (NON-BLOCKING, informational, outside my scope and outside this diff). registry.json /runs/57/note still cross-references "that handoff's orch_reconstruction field", a key name that no longer exists after the 3e rename. Stale pointer only; the file it points at is unambiguous and its new name is documented. Not fixable here (I am scoped to two handoff files) and NOT worth a rework iteration.
N4 (NON-BLOCKING, advisory, no action needed). anti-patterns.md:1018 "Trace the four steps" sits in an entry that already uses "four steps" at :984 for the numbered propagation list, while the sentence that follows names three levels (count / class / exclusion set). Defensible as written -- the parenthetical "(four keys, three deaths)" carries the count-and-unit level as two -- so I am NOT calling it an error; recording it only because a numeric ambiguity inside the paragraph that teaches numeric care is the kind of thing a later reader may trip on.

Nothing above is blocking. Not one of N1-N4 makes a rule WRONG, and not one would lead an agent to a wrong classification of any incident on record or any incident of the shapes now described. I applied the blocking test honestly rather than deferentially: had the amended membership test still excluded a table row, or had the ISS-0109 file failed to conform to its own normative table, or had the exclusion sentence still read as exhaustive, I would have FAILed and accepted the ESCALATION.

=== THE STEP-03d POSTSCRIPT -- DONE, APPEND-ONLY, VERIFIED BY STRUCTURAL DIFF ===
I accept ORCH's ruling and withdraw my Step 3f refusal: 4.1's prohibition is against a SECOND PARTY writing an agent's result and against a SILENT rewrite, and an attesting agent appending a MARKED correction to its own attestation is neither. Appended to handoffs/WF03-ISS0117-20260821/step-03d-reviewer-regate.json's result.summary, behind an explicit "=== CORRECTION POSTSCRIPT -- APPENDED 2026-08-21 BY REVIEWER ITSELF AT WF-03 STEP 3h. EVERYTHING ABOVE THIS DELIMITER IS UNALTERED. ===" delimiter, stating in its own words that it is an append.

I did not take the two corrected figures on trust either -- I re-measured both myself before attesting to them. next_action as a TOP-LEVEL key over all 553 handoff *.json at 57fd10d: SIX files, enumerated by path in the postscript (WF02-REQ033/step-01-code-designer, WF02-REQ051/step-05-release-validator, WF02-REQ051/step-06-doc-updater, WF03-ISS0047/step-02-code-designer, WF03-ISS0047/step-04-test-designer, WF03-ISS0047/step-05-issue-fixer) -- refuting my five. Same-day boundary at 0bbb2cc: 46 files with a 2026-08-21 created_at, of which 42 predate 131aba9 (2026-08-21T12:13:08+05:00 = 07:13:08Z) -- reproducing DOC-UPDATER's pair exactly and refuting my 45/43. Also measured at 57fd10d: same-day 48, predating 42 -- the same-day total grows with this very run while the 42 is stable, which is the concrete demonstration that the boundary had to be a COMMIT and not a day. The postscript records that the protocol text as committed needs no change: it already carries the correct figures; what was wrong was my arithmetic, not the artefact I was gating.

APPEND-ONLY CONFIRMED BY DIFFING THE PARSED STRUCTURE, quoted: with result.summary masked on both sides, `after == before` -> True; `after['result']['summary'].startswith(old)` -> True; summary 22123 -> 24369 chars (+2246, all at the tail); result.status PASS unchanged; status COMPLETED unchanged; created_at 2026-08-21T07:39:10Z / started_at 07:39:10Z / completed_at 07:45:46Z all unchanged; `after['result']['issues'] == before['result']['issues']` -> True (4 entries); `after['task'] == before['task']` -> True (7906 chars, ORCH's restored block left exactly as it stood, untouched); top-level key order identical. The edit was made by string-substituting the single JSON string literal in the raw file rather than by re-serialising the document, so no reformatting could leak in: `git diff --numstat` on that file -> `1	1`, one line changed, and that line is the summary line.

=== VERDICT AND BUDGET STANDING ===
PASS. REWORK BUDGET: 2 of max_rework 3 used -- one iteration remains, and this PASS does not spend it. I am stating plainly that the budget did NOT decide this verdict: the four gated items are each verified against the artefacts first-hand, the one item that required a genuine ruling (DOC-UPDATER's departure from my own proposed test) is upheld because it is correct and my formulation was not, and the four residual findings are text-precision items that leave every rule right and every classification decidable. Had any of them been blocking I would have FAILed into ESCALATED, because a wrong rule in this corpus outlives a stopped run.
`git status --porcelain` at completion: ` M docs/issues/ISS-0192.yaml` and `?? docs/issues/ISS-0196.yaml` (both ORCH's, deliberately untouched and never staged), plus the two handoff files this step wrote. No file under docs/ was modified by me; no gh call and no queue call was made.
